from.place: Current main-20261015 proof opening 'Choose a compactification c=(j,p)': arbitrary-site descent foundation for the affine-local compactification repair; bounded-below hypersheaf model steps 4-5: small hypercover test maps generate all cohomology-sheaf equivalences; the structural generation theorem is below the local-object characterization. Supporting primitive: Localized free Dold--Kan adjunction for module presheaves.

title: Localized free Dold--Kan adjunction for module presheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows into an object closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. No fibre products or subcanonicity are assumed. Use [def-weil-size-convention] for universes and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] for associated sheaves.

Write $h_T(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,T)$. A hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$ is an augmented simplicial presheaf of sets whose terms are small coproducts of representables and whose augmented matching maps become epimorphisms after sheafification. The degree-zero matching presheaf is $h_T$; all higher matching presheaves, parametrizing compatible proper faces, are formed in presheaves. A refinement over $T$ means a morphism of augmented simplicial presheaves over $h_T$. A collection is dense if every hypercover over every $T$ admits a refinement by a member of that collection over the same $T$.

Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda)$, with unbounded cochains as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$ write $L_T=\Lambda[h_T]$ and let $e_U:A_U\to L_T[0]$ be the alternating-face augmentation, where $A_U^{-n}=\Lambda[U_n]$ for $n\ge0$ and $A_U^r=0$ for $r>0$. Let $H$ be any small set of these hypercovers, not assumed dense, and let $B=\{e_U[k]:U\in H,\ k\in\mathbf Z\}$. Give $\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal P)$ its projective model and $B$-localized model [lem-cbc-dg-presheaf-model-localizations]. Give simplicial presheaves $\mathsf U(\mathcal C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sSet})$ their projective model and its left Bousfield localization at the augmentation maps in $H$ [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-localization-comparison], using simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set].

Let $N\Lambda$ take objectwise free simplicial $\Lambda$-modules, then their normalized nonnegative chain complexes $N_n=\bigcap_{i=1}^n\ker(d_i)$ with differential $d_0$, and reindex chain degree $n$ as cochain degree $-n$. Let $R(K)$ be the underlying simplicial presheaf of the Dold--Kan inverse of the nonnegative chain complex obtained by reindexing the smart truncation $\tau^{\le0}K$, whose term at $0$ is $\ker(d_K^0)$ and whose negative terms are those of $K$. These functors form an adjunction $N\Lambda\dashv R$ which is Quillen both for the projective models and for the localized models $\mathsf U(\mathcal C)_H\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal P)_B$.

The presheaf $R(K)$ is objectwise Kan and $\pi_m(R(K)(V),0)=H^{-m}(K(V))$ for $m\ge1$, while $\pi_0(R(K)(V))$ is the underlying set of $H^0(K(V))$. Translations identify the homotopy groups at any other vertex with those at zero, naturally on the corresponding slice site. The functor $R$ sends every cohomology-sheaf equivalence of complexes to a local weak equivalence of simplicial presheaves. A Kan complex is a simplicial set with fillers for all horns. The standard simplex $\Delta^n$ is the simplicial set represented by $[n]$, its boundary $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of its proper faces, and a horn is the union of all faces except one. For objectwise Kan simplicial presheaves, a local weak equivalence means an isomorphism on the associated sheaves of $\pi_0$ and, for every $V\in\mathcal C$, vertex $x\in X(V)_0$ and $m\ge1$, an isomorphism on the associated sheaves on $\mathcal C/V$ of the homotopy groups $\pi_m(X|_{\mathcal C/V},x)\to\pi_m(Y|_{\mathcal C/V},f(x))$. Here $\mathcal C/V$ has the induced covering-sieve topology.

For every $T$, the map $N\Lambda(h_T\times\partial\Delta^1)\to N\Lambda(h_T\times\Delta^1)$ is the inclusion $L_T[0]\oplus L_T[0]\to I_T$, where $I_T^{-1}=L_T$, $I_T^0=L_T\oplus L_T$, its differential sends $a$ to $(-a,a)$, and all other terms vanish. Thus the endpoint inclusion is identified under the same adjunction, including its maps, with the simplicial boundary inclusion.
